_comment: One entry per quantization arm of the same model family. `dir` is a directory under MODELS_DIR and is what the engine serves: turboderp's EXL3 variants are branches of one repo, and the engine's cache resolver falls back to the newest config-bearing snapshot when refs/main carries no weights, so a repo id would serve whichever variant was downloaded last.

nvfp4-swift.note: the rig's baseline arm, served from the HF cache; the engine prints its untested-checkpoint notice for it

nvfp4-local-inference-lab.note: in the engine's tested list; 106 GB, i.e. a different face/table treatment than ukisai's 186 GB

nvfp4-nvidia.note: the vendor's own ModelOpt export of this family; not in the engine's tested list yet, so measure before trusting it

exl3-405-turboderp.format: exl3 mul1 4.05bpw, head 6, MTP 4, n-gram rows at 6 bits
exl3-405-turboderp.note: 68.3 GB of shards + 39.04 GB of n-gram rows in one I16[320001536,61] tensor (1 scale + 160x6 bits = the engine's NgramTable codec); MTP head quantized in shard 9; published mean KL vs BF16 0.0067

exl3-605-turboderp.note: the near-lossless anchor arm (published KL 0.0031, noise floor 0.00249); 139 GB, so it streams more of itself

exl3-305-turboderp.format: exl3 mul1 3.05bpw, n-gram rows at 5 bits
exl3-305-turboderp.note: the only variant that also quantizes the n-gram table (32.6 GB against 39.04), so it prices the retrieval path separately; published KL 0.0177
